title: About
text: POLI 450A is the first course in the political science PhD methods sequence at Stanford University. The course was originally designed by Jens Hainmueller and is maintained and updated by Yiqing Xu, Department of Political Science, Stanford University. This version is from Fall 2026.

title: About
text:
How the materials were checked
Before a lecture entered the repository, it went through a release review. The numbers on the slides were rerun from the code, the citations were checked against their sources, and independent readers went through each deck line by line, with the fixes applied.

title: About
text:
Data
The examples use public data: U.S. election returns and Census data, the American National Election Studies, the Cooperative Election Study, V-Dem and World Bank data, the Brexit vote, and replication data from published studies. SOURCES.md lists every data file, where it comes from, and its terms.

title: Teaching with the slides
text: You are welcome to teach with these slides, in whole or in part, and to adapt them for your own course.

title: Teaching with the slides
text:
License

The slides, their LaTeX sources, the worksheets, the original figures, and the videos are licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0. You may copy, adapt and teach with them, with credit, but not for commercial purposes.
The R code is licensed under the MIT License.
The data files keep their own terms, listed with their sources in SOURCES.md.

title: Teaching with the slides
text:
Teaching with the videos
In class, we play a video one part at a time and explain each concept, sometimes pausing mid-part to settle a conceptual question. We then turn to the slides for the details and work through worksheet questions with the students at the whiteboard. A silent page between two parts of a video names the slide where the next part starts, so that you can pause there and open the slides. The videos are in one YouTube playlist.

title: Teaching with the slides
text:
Materials for instructors
Problem sets with solutions, worksheet solutions, and past exams are available to instructors on request. Please email yiqingxu@stanford.edu from your institutional address, name the course you teach, and do not post the solutions publicly.

title: Teaching with the slides
text:
Building and adapting the slides
Each lecture’s folder in the repository holds the LaTeX Beamer source, the figures, the R scripts that draw them, and the data the scripts read. All lectures share one template, lectures/course_preamble.tex and lectures/course_theme.tex, and every R script uses the shared figure style in lectures/course_figures.R. You need TeX Live 2023 or later and R 4.x. The README has the build commands.

title: Teaching with the slides
text:
Corrections
Comments and corrections are welcome as issues on GitHub.

title: POLI 450A: Political Methodology I (Regression)
text:
Lecture slides, worksheets, short videos, R code and data for the first course in Stanford’s political science PhD methods sequence. The course also suits advanced undergraduates in economics, political science, and other social sciences. The course covers point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing, simple and multiple regression, and robust and clustered standard errors. The R scripts in the repository draw the figures and print the numbers on the slides from public data. The syllabus lists the topics, readings, and course policies, including the policy on generative AI.
The slides have one page per slide. To present with the step-by-step reveals, build that version from the LaTeX source. The worksheets are the in-class exercises. Each lecture title opens the lecture’s folder on GitHub: the LaTeX source, the figures, the R scripts that draw them, and the data.
Each lecture also has a video of five to twelve minutes, all in one YouTube playlist. The videos are designed to be conceptual and intuitive. Each presents the main ideas, one or two real examples, and the numbers from the lecture’s R code; the details of the mathematical derivations are covered in class.

title: POLI 450A: Political Methodology I (Regression)
text:
Pedagogy
The videos pin down the conceptual issues, so that class time can go to the worksheet questions, the mathematics, and deeper insights. In class, we watch each video in segments, one part at a time, so that each concept is tied directly to its mathematical derivation and to examples. Between segments, we pause to settle conceptual questions, turn to the slides for the derivations, and work through worksheet questions with the students at the whiteboard. Outside class, students can watch a video before the lecture as a preview and again afterwards as a review.

title: POLI 450A: Political Methodology I (Regression)
text:
Prerequisites
Linear algebra and calculus at the level of a political science math camp, and some undergraduate probability, statistics and statistical computing. The course uses R.
